prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name a single “best” broker for Kansas City (that’s subjective and changes over time), but I can help you find a highly qualified local broker and tell you exactly how to choose one.

Quick summary
- Use licensed, independent brokers when possible (they compare multiple insurers).
- Verify licensing in Missouri and/or Kansas depending on your ZIP code.
- Look for AHIP certification for Medicare help and Marketplace experience for ACA plans.
- Check reviews on Google/Yelp/BBB and ask for references.
- If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is for individual/family, small business, or Medicare, and I’ll help tailor next steps.

Where to find qualified brokers
- HealthCare.gov “Find local help” (in-person navigators and brokers for ACA plans).
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance and Kansas Insurance Department — both have license lookup tools so you can confirm a broker’s license and any complaints.
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool.
- Medicare.gov “Find local help” or the plan finder (for Medicare-specific agents).
- Google/Yelp/Better Business Bureau for reviews of local firms.

What to prefer and what to verify
- Independent vs captive: Independent brokers represent multiple carriers and can compare plans; captive agents sell only one carrier’s products.
- Licensing: Must be licensed for health insurance in the state where you live (and both MO and KS if you cross state lines).
- Certification: AHIP training is a common sign an agent is current for Medicare products; ask about specific Marketplace or small-group experience for ACA/small-employer plans.
- Compensation: Most brokers are paid by the insurer, so services are often free to you — confirm upfront.
- Conflicts: Ask whether they receive incentives to push a particular carrier.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- How long have you helped clients in Kansas City with plans like mine?
- Are you licensed in Missouri/Kansas (whichever applies)? Can you show your license number?
- Are you independent or do you represent specific insurers?
- Have you helped clients enroll in Marketplace/Medicaid/Medicare/small-group plans (whichever applies)?
- What do you charge (if anything)?
- Can you provide references from recent clients?
- Will you help with claims or plan changes after enrollment?

What to bring / information to provide when you meet
- ZIP code and household count
- Ages and any dependent info
- Current coverage and policy numbers (if any)
- Income estimate for Marketplace eligibility (household modified adjusted gross income)
- List of preferred doctors and prescriptions (for network and drug-check)
- Employer info if small-group plan

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short phone/email script to contact brokers.
- Help you narrow options if you give your ZIP code and type of plan (individual/family, small-business, Medicare).
Tell me your ZIP code and which kind of plan you need and I’ll help you find the right questions and prepare a shortlist strategy.
